rows.notes: The cited work is FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev.1, a field guide/guideline synthesising reported experience from many sources (preface: guidelines based on reported experiences; tables adapted from Maas, Rhoades, Nakayama, WHO etc.). It reports no data, experiment, survey or model of its own; the case summaries in Section 8 are second-hand summaries citing other reports (Savva et al., Rhoades, Tanji, etc.). The statement relevant to the claim appears in Section 7 (wastewater re-use): ridge-and-furrow systems contaminate neither air nor upper plant parts, subsurface tile or trickle systems create the fewest hazards of any kind, sprinklers create the greatest potential for microbial contamination of vegetation and air; it also notes trickle systems are expensive at large scale and prone to clogging with effluent. This is an unsupported guideline assertion, not an own result, so Q1 is no and Q2-Q9 are no.

notes: Document is a complete FAO guideline publication (non-primary). The passage's content is traceable to Section 7, but as a general statement drawn from the literature rather than from any data generated by the authors.
